info.title: CanvasNet Tool
info.description: DemaConsulting.CanvasNet.Tool is the canvasnet command-line tool: it inspects, renders, and transforms images and documents (PNG, JPEG, BMP, TIFF, GIF, JPEG 2000, SVG, PDF, PowerPoint, Visio, OpenSCAD models, and Vega-Lite charts) using the CanvasNet libraries, with a stable machine-readable JSON contract so that scripts and AI agents can drive it.

commands.name: compare
commands.description: Measure how much two images differ (MAE, RMSE, PSNR, SSIM), and draw the differences

options.name: --page
options.description: The page or slide to render, counted from 1 (default 1)

options.name: --dpi
options.description: Resolution of a PDF, PPTX, or VSDX page in dots per inch (default 96; VSDX needs a whole number)

options.name: --a-page
options.description: The page or slide of the first input, counted from 1 (a document only; overrides --page)

options.name: --b-page
options.description: The page or slide of the second input, counted from 1 (a document only; overrides --page)

options.name: --a-dpi
options.description: Resolution of the first input in dots per inch (a document only; overrides --dpi)

options.name: --b-dpi
options.description: Resolution of the second input in dots per inch (a document only; overrides --dpi)

options.name: --background
options.description: Opaque color that transparency is flattened over: white (default), black, #RRGGBB, or a color name

options.name: --no-auto-orient
options.description: Do not turn a JPEG upright according to its EXIF orientation

options.name: --strict
options.description: Fail with unsupported-feature instead of skipping a picture or shape the library cannot draw

options.name: --view
options.description: SCAD model: the viewpoint - iso (default; top for a model that is entirely 2D), front, back, left, right, top, or bottom

options.name: --azimuth
options.description: SCAD model: replace the azimuth of the view, in degrees about the Z axis (0 = from the front)

options.name: --elevation
options.description: SCAD model: replace the elevation of the view, in degrees above the XY plane (-90 to 90)

options.name: --projection
options.description: SCAD model: ortho (default) or perspective

options.name: --define
options.description: SCAD model: set a variable, for example -D width=20 or -D label=text (repeatable)

options.name: --time
options.description: SCAD model: the value of $t, the animation time (default 0)

options.name: --default-color
options.description: SCAD model: the color of surfaces the model does not color (default gray)

options.name: --max-triangles
options.description: SCAD model: the most triangles the model may produce (default 5000000)

options.name: --a-view
options.description: SCAD model: the viewpoint of the first input (overrides --view)

options.name: --b-view
options.description: SCAD model: the viewpoint of the second input (overrides --view)

options.name: --a-define
options.description: SCAD model: set a variable of the first input (repeatable; wins over -D of the same name)

options.name: --b-define
options.description: SCAD model: set a variable of the second input (repeatable; wins over -D of the same name)

options.name: --resize-to
options.description: Bring both inputs to one size: a (the size of the first input), b (the second), or WxH

options.name: --fit
options.description: How a raster input is fitted to --resize-to: contain (default; keeps the aspect ratio, with margins) or stretch

options.name: --filter
options.description: Resampling filter of a resize or fit: auto (default), nearest, bilinear, bicubic, lanczos3, or area

options.name: --tolerance
options.description: A pixel differs when a channel differs by more than this, 0-255 (default 8)

options.name: --grid
options.description: Report the error of each cell of a grid, columns x rows, each 1-64 (default 4x4)

options.name: --threshold
options.description: Fail (exit code 1) unless a metric is within a limit: mae, rmse, max-diff, diff-ratio, or cell-rmse at most; psnr or ssim at least (repeatable)

options.name: --diff
options.description: Write a picture of the differences to this file

options.name: --diff-style
options.description: How --diff draws a difference: heat (default) or abs; --side-by-side always uses heat

options.name: --gain
options.description: Amplification of a difference in the pictures, 0.1-255 (default 4)

options.name: --side-by-side
options.description: Write the first input, the second input, and the differences side by side to this file

options.name: --overlay
options.description: Write a blend of both inputs to this file

options.name: --overlay-weight
options.description: Weight of the second input in --overlay, 0-1 (default 0.5)

options.name: --quality
options.description: JPEG quality, 1-100 (default 90)

options.name: --no-clobber
options.description: Fail instead of overwriting an existing output file

options.description: Display version information

options.name: --grayscale

options.name: --invert
options.description: Invert the colors; transparency is kept

options.name: --threshold
options.description: Turn the image black and white: pixels with a luma above the level (0-255) become white; auto chooses the level with Otsu's method

options.name: --levels
options.description: Map the levels black..white to 0..255, with an optional gamma (0.1-10; above 1 brightens the midtones), for example 20,230 or 20,230,1.2

options.name: --brightness
options.description: Add an amount (-255 to 255) to every color level

options.name: --contrast
options.description: Change the contrast around mid-gray by a percentage (-100 to 100)

options.name: --auto-levels
options.description: Stretch the levels so the darkest and lightest pixels become black and white (ignoring 1% of the pixels at each end; see --auto-levels-clip)

options.name: --auto-levels-clip
options.description: Percentage of the pixels --auto-levels ignores at each end, 0-20 (default 1)

options.name: --deskew
options.description: Straighten the image: find the tilt of its near-horizontal lines (within 15 degrees) and rotate it level; the angle is in the --json result

options.name: --trim
options.description: Crop away the uniform border around the content (the background is the most common color of the four corners)

options.name: --trim-tolerance
options.description: How far a pixel may differ from the background and still count as background, 0-255 (default 8)

options.name: --grid
options.description: Draw a labeled coordinate grid with a line every N pixels (8-4096) in the color given (default #FF00FFA0); put it last to read the final coordinates

commands.name: json
commands.description:
With --json every command writes exactly one JSON document, on
one line, to standard output.

commands.name: anchors
commands.description:
Only for an OpenSCAD model: the points it declared with echo("anchor",
"name", [x, y, z]), in echo order, each {name, point: [x, y, z], pixel:
[x, y] or null, inside}. pixel is the position in the written picture,
from its top-left corner, after the pixel steps; see 'canvasnet help
scad'.

commands.name: code
commands.description:
The stable identifier of the feature, for example scad-module-surface or
vl-mark-geoshape. A warning of a SCAD model has the code scad-warning; a
warning of a Vega-Lite chart has the code vega-lite-warning and carries
its vl-* identifier at the start of the message text.

commands.name: compare
commands.description:
Described in their own help: run 'canvasnet help compare', 'canvasnet
help montage', or 'canvasnet help inspect'.

commands.name: diagnostics
commands.description:
The features that were left out of the picture; see the diagnostics
section below.

commands.name: echo
commands.description: The text an OpenSCAD model printed with echo.

commands.name: error
commands.description:
{code, message, hint}: code is one of the stable codes of the errors
topic ('canvasnet help errors'); hint is omitted when there is none. The
document has no exit-code field: the exit code of every failure is 1.
- A failure document is written only when --json is given and --silent is
not. A failed compare gate also carries the fields of the comparison.

commands.name: formats
commands.description:
tool, library, inputs[], outputs[], quality {min, max, default}, and
maxDimension. Each inputs[] entry has format, kind, extensions,
multiPage, vector, and helpTopic: the topic of 'canvasnet help <topic>'
that describes the format (raster for png, jpeg, bmp, tiff, gif, and
jpeg2000).

commands.name: help
commands.description:
kind is index, command, topic, examples, or example; see the help
section below.

commands.name: info
commands.description:
input {path, format, bytes} and one of image, document {pageCount,
pages[]}, model {modules, functions, directives}, or chart (after an
image object with the laid-out size).

commands.name: input
commands.description:
{path, format, natural: {width, height}}, and for a document pageCount
and page.

commands.name: message
commands.description: A description; for a model or chart it gives file, line, and column.

commands.name: operations
commands.description:
Every step that was applied, in order; each has an op key (render,
embed, auto-orient, resize, fit, flatten, crop, rotate, flip, pad, and
the photo operations) and its own fields. With --all-pages every
operation also carries its page. The verbs are crop, resize, rotate,
flip, and pad.

commands.name: outputs
commands.description:
One entry per file written: {path, format, width, height, bytes} and
page for a document.

commands.name: page
commands.description:
The page of a document the report belongs to.
- Without --json the same reports are written to standard error as
'Unsupported: <code>: <message>' or 'Warning: <code>: <message>' lines
(and echo as 'ECHO: <text>'); with --json standard error carries none of
them, so standard output stays one JSON document.

commands.name: severity
commands.description:
unsupported for a feature that was left out, or warning for a
questionable construct that still rendered.

commands.name: source
commands.description:
Where the report comes from: scad, vega-lite, pptx, vsdx, or svg. PDF
and raster images have no diagnostics channel.

commands.name: tool
commands.description: {name, version} of the tool.

commands.name: limits

each one produces.

options.description:
Accepted, but PDF has no diagnostics channel, so it changes nothing.
Diagnostics and --strict:
- None: the diagnostics[] list of a PDF is always empty and --strict has no
effect. A feature the renderer cannot draw is an error instead.
unsupported-feature
Error code: the message names the feature, for example
pdf-image-lab-decode or pdf-image-tint-budget.
corrupt-input
Error code: a damaged or truncated document.
page-out-of-range
Error code: --page is beyond the last page.
Known differences from PDF viewers:
- ICC profiles are not applied, so colors in ICCBased spaces can differ
slightly from a viewer.
- A substituted font is chosen from the installed fonts, so text with fonts
that are not embedded can differ between machines.

approximated: each vertex is converted to RGB first and the result is
blended.

than dropped.

commands.name: scad
commands.description:
A model is evaluated and drawn as one still picture from a named
viewpoint.

options.name: --view
options.description:
The viewpoint: iso (default; a model that is entirely 2D defaults to
top), front, back, left, right, top, or bottom.

options.name: --azimuth
options.description:
Replace the azimuth of the view: degrees about the Z axis, 0 from the
front.

options.name: --elevation
options.description:
Replace the elevation of the view: degrees above the XY plane, -90 to
90.

options.name: --projection
options.description: ortho (default) or perspective.

options.name: --define
options.description:
Set a variable of the model; -D is the short form. Repeatable; the later
definition wins.

options.name: --time
options.description: The value of $t (default 0).

options.name: --default-color
options.description:
The color of surfaces the model does not color (default gray); the alpha
is ignored. A flat 2D drawing is gray by default, so --default-color
black gives a high-contrast drawing; a color() in the model overrides
it.

options.name: --max-triangles
options.description: The most triangles the model may produce (default 5000000).

options.name: --size
options.description:
The picture is 800x800 pixels unless a size option is given; --width,
--height, and --scale also size it. The camera fits the picture; nothing
is stretched.

options.name: --background
options.description:
The color the picture is flattened over (default white; black, #RRGGBB,
or #RRGGBBAA); transparent keeps alpha.

options.name: --strict
options.description:
Fail with unsupported-feature instead of leaving a construct out.
Diagnostics and --strict:
- Without --strict an unsupported construct is left out and listed in
diagnostics[] of the JSON result as {source: scad, severity: unsupported,
code: <id>} (without --json, as an 'Unsupported: <id>: <message>' line on
standard error). With --strict the first one fails with
unsupported-feature and no file is written.
- The output of echo() is in echo[] of the JSON result as 'ECHO: <text>'
lines; without --json it is written to standard error in the same form.
scad-module-offset
Also scad-module-surface, scad-module-import, and scad-module-roof: the
module and its children are omitted.
scad-projection-too-complex
A projection needs more work than one projection may do (too many
triangles, or a difference or an intersection whose silhouette costs too
much to classify): the projection is omitted.
scad-projection-open-mesh
A projection found a mesh that is not a closed solid (its cross-section
does not close): the projection is omitted.
scad-hull-csg-operand
A hull has a difference or an intersection among its children.
scad-hull-mixed-dimensions
A hull has both 2D and 3D children.
scad-minkowski-nonconvex
A minkowski has a child that is not convex.
scad-minkowski-2d
A minkowski of 2D children.
scad-minkowski-mixed-dimensions
A minkowski has both 2D and 3D children.
scad-modifier-highlight
# on a 2D shape that is not extruded: drawn normally, without highlight.
scad-modifier-background
% on a 2D shape that is not extruded: omitted.
scad-multmatrix-projective
multmatrix with a bottom row other than [0, 0, 0, 1]: omitted.
scad-resize-approximate
resize over children that contain a difference or an intersection:
estimated bounds are used.
scad-function-<name>
An unimplemented built-in function, for example
scad-function-textmetrics: the call evaluates to undef.
scad-warning
Severity warning: a questionable argument (an invalid argument, for
example) that still renders.
scad-error
Error code: a syntax error, an evaluation error, or an include that
cannot be read; the message names file, line, and column.
budget-exceeded
Error code: the model needs more triangles than --max-triangles allows.
- See the OpenSCAD section of the Scad user guide for the complete list of
identifiers.
Anchors (callout points):
- echo("anchor", "name", [x, y, z]); declares a named point of the model,
for a callout or a leader line drawn on the picture later. The echo line
is still printed. The point is in the coordinate system where the
statement stands: every enclosing translate, rotate, scale, mirror, and
multmatrix is applied, so the anchor is a world point. Only the statement
form counts; an echo used as an expression, or inside a function, is a
plain echo.
- A module, for, if, union, difference, intersection, render, color, hull,
or minkowski does not move its children, so the point passes through
unchanged. An anchor inside resize, linear_extrude, rotate_extrude,
projection, or another module that cannot give its children a position is
skipped with a scad-anchor-invalid warning.
scad-anchor-invalid
Severity warning (code scad-warning, the identifier starts the message):
a malformed declaration (a name that is not a non-empty string, a point
that is not three finite numbers, a named or an extra argument) or an
anchor in an unsupported context. The anchor is skipped; the echo line
stays.
- The same name may be declared more than once; every declaration is kept,
in echo order.
- With --json, render adds anchors[] for a model: {name, point: [x, y, z],
pixel: [x, y], inside}. pixel is the position in the written picture in
pixels from its top-left corner (continuous: pixel i spans [i, i+1), so
the center of the first pixel is 0.5), projected with the camera that drew
the picture, perspective included. inside is true when pixel lies within
the picture. Without --json nothing is added.
- The pixel steps move the anchors with the picture: --crop, --trim,
--resize, --fit, --pad, --flip, and --rotate are applied to pixel, and
inside is tested against the final picture. After a --deskew that corrects
the image, pixel is null; it is also null for a point behind a perspective
camera (inside is then false).
- pixel says where a point projects, not whether it can be seen: an anchor
hidden behind other geometry still has a pixel and inside true.
Known differences from OpenSCAD:
- This is an independent dialect, not OpenSCAD: pictures and tessellation
are not pixel-identical to OpenSCAD and no parity is claimed.
- include and use are read only from the model's folder and below, symbolic
links are not followed, and a missing include is an error here.
- A model can be drawn inside an SVG diagram with <image href="part.scad"
.../> (see 'canvasnet help svg'), with the view the library chooses for it
(isometric for a 3D model, top-down for a flat 2D model, or the model's
own $vp* variables) over a transparent background.
- Indexing is lenient: v[i] is undef for a negative or non-finite index, and
a fractional index is truncated.
- text() is laid out one character at a time without shaping or ligatures;
language and script are ignored; size is the height of the glyph H. A
generic name (sans, serif, mono, sans-serif, monospace, ...) is a bundled
Liberation font; any other family is looked up in the installed fonts (so
it can differ between machines), then among the bundled Liberation
families, and a family found nowhere is drawn with the bundled Liberation
Sans and a warning. For each character the chosen font lacks, the glyph
comes from the bundled Noto Sans, Noto Sans Math, or Noto Sans Symbols 2
(never an installed font), with no kerning across fonts; characters
nothing covers are listed in one warning per text().
- The semantics of the # highlight and the % ghost are this package's
documented choices; a ghost is part of the fitted bounds but not of the
model.
- hull and minkowski constructs they cannot handle are omitted and reported,
never approximated; so is a projection that is too complex or whose mesh
is not closed.
- projection(cut = true) includes a face that lies exactly in the z = 0
plane (a closed section); the silhouette and the section are computed from
the tessellated meshes, so a curved solid projects to its polygon.
- The viewport variables follow the documented meaning of the OpenSCAD ones
($vpr is the rotation of the camera, so rotate($vpr) turns an object to
face it). The model sees the default $vpt = [0, 0, 0], $vpd = 140, and
$vpf = 22.5 and the $vpr of the requested view, because the camera is
fitted after the model is built; only an assignment of $vpt, $vpd, or $vpf
turns off the automatic framing.
- The result is a static picture from a named view (iso by default, top for
a model that is entirely 2D; orthographic by default), not an interactive
camera.

commands.name: svg
commands.description:
A common subset of SVG, drawn sharply at the target size. An
image can embed a picture, a model, a chart, or another SVG file
that sits in the same folder.

options.name: --width
options.description:
Draw at this width, keeping the aspect ratio; --height does the same for
the height. The drawing is sharp, never enlarged afterwards.

options.name: --size
options.description: Draw inside this box, centered and never stretched.

options.name: --scale
options.description: Multiply the intrinsic size by a factor.

options.name: --background
options.description:
The color transparency is flattened over (white by default); transparent
keeps alpha.

options.name: --strict
options.description:
An image that was not drawn (svg-image-unresolved or
svg-image-too-large) is an unsupported-feature error instead of a
warning, and so is an unsupported feature of an embedded model or chart.
Diagnostics and --strict:
svg-image-unresolved
Warning: an image href was not drawn. The message names the href and
why: not found, outside the folder, a network URL, a format the tool
cannot draw, a cycle, or a limit. With --strict it is an
unsupported-feature error.
svg-image-too-large
Warning: an image was not drawn because its picture does not fit in the
pixel budget of the render. The message names the href and the pixels it
needs. With --strict it is an unsupported-feature error.
- The notes of an embedded model, chart, or SVG file are reported too, each
starting with the href of the file, and the lines an embedded model prints
with echo are kept.
- An embedded file that is found but is broken (a corrupt picture, a model
with a syntax error, a chart with a bad specification) is an error with
its own code, and the message names both files.
corrupt-input
Error code: malformed XML, a root element that is not svg, or a document
over a limit.
Known differences from browsers:
- No scripting, animation, or network resources; images are read only from
the folder of the SVG file, and only by the command line tool (the library
opts in with SvgLoadOptions.ImageResolver).
- Text is best effort without shaping. An installed family is used, so text
can differ between machines; generic and unknown families use the bundled
Liberation fonts. A character those lack (such as U+221D) is taken from
the bundled Noto fonts; a character nothing covers draws the font's
missing-glyph box with no diagnostic, because SVG rendering reports
nothing.
- The drawing is rendered sharply at the target size, not rasterized first
and scaled afterwards.

commands.name: vega-lite
commands.description:
A chart is laid out and drawn as one still picture; a defined
subset of Vega-Lite 5 and 6.

options.name: --scale
options.description: Multiply the laid-out size by a factor.

options.name: --width
options.description:
Fit the chart to a width, keeping its aspect ratio; --height does the
same for the height.

options.name: --size
options.description: Fit the chart inside a box and center it.

options.name: --background
options.description:
Replace the background the chart declares (white when it declares none);
transparent keeps alpha.

options.name: --strict
options.description: Fail with unsupported-feature instead of leaving a construct out.

options.name: --page
options.description:
A chart has one page, so only 1 is valid; a larger number is
page-out-of-range.
- The model options (-D, --view, ...) are a usage-error for a chart.
'canvasnet info' reports the laid-out size, marks, and data references
without drawing.
Diagnostics and --strict:
- Identifiers have the form vl-<area>-<detail>, in lower case. An
unsupported construct is listed in diagnostics[] as {source: vega-lite,
severity: unsupported, code: <id>} (without --json, also as an
'Unsupported: <id>: <message>' line on standard error); the message gives
file, line, column, and JSON pointer. With --strict the first one fails
with unsupported-feature.
vl-mark-<type>
A mark that is not drawn, for example vl-mark-geoshape; the view is
drawn without marks.
vl-channel-geo
A longitude or latitude channel.
vl-data-remote-url
A url with a scheme, a drive letter, or an absolute path: never fetched,
empty dataset.
vl-data-geo
Geographic data (sphere, graticule, topojson).
vl-projection
A projection.
vl-param-selection
A selection param: nothing is selected.
vl-param-variable
A variable param of a nested view (a layer or a composition).
vl-transform-<name>
A transform that is not run, for example vl-transform-regression.
vl-expr-function-<name>
An expression function outside the supported 100, for example
vl-expr-function-now: the call evaluates to null.
vl-guide-encode
axis.encode or legend.encode.
vl-offset-position
An xOffset or yOffset that has no nominal or ordinal x or y channel (or
a temporal one with a time unit that can hold it) to nest in: the offset
is ignored.
vl-offset-ranged
A quantitative or temporal xOffset or yOffset of a bar or area (a ranged
offset): the offset is ignored.
vl-shape-path
A custom SVG-path shape: a circle is drawn.
vl-scale-<type>
A scale type that is not supported, for example vl-scale-identity.
vl-type-geojson
The geojson field type.
vl-unknown-property
Warning: a property Vega-Lite does not define for that object.
vl-schema-version
Warning: a $schema that is not version 5 or 6; version 6 defaults are
used.
vl-layout-fit-step
Warning: autosize fit together with a step size; the fit is dropped for
that dimension.
vl-composition-property-ignored
Warning: a width, height, padding, config, or similar property of a
composition that only the top-level view decides.
vl-text-missing-glyph
Warning: text with characters that neither the font nor the bundled
fallback fonts have a glyph for (for example a private-use or CJK
character); the font's missing-glyph box is drawn. Reported at the text
mark, or with no location for axis labels, legends, and titles.
- Warnings have the code vega-lite-warning and carry the vl-* identifier at
the start of the message text, after the location. Errors: vega-lite-error
(invalid specification, a data file that is missing or refused, a chart
that cannot be drawn), budget-exceeded (a library limit), corrupt-input (a
specification longer than 4194304 characters), and size-limit (a chart
laid out beyond 8192 pixels on a side).
- See the Vega-Lite section of the Vega-Lite user guide for the complete
list of identifiers.
Known differences from Vega-Lite:
- The picture is static: no interaction, and tooltips are omitted.
- A schema of version 5 is drawn with the version 6 defaults (a view is 300
by 300 pixels by default, for example).
- Text is measured with the bundled fonts, so labels, legends, and facet
headers can differ from a browser by a few pixels. A character the
Liberation fonts lack is drawn from the bundled Noto fonts, never from an
installed font, so the result does not depend on the machine.
- Dates are always UTC; nothing is read from the network; data files are
only read from the specification's folder and below.
- A chart can be drawn inside an SVG diagram with <image
href="chart.vl.json" .../> (see 'canvasnet help svg'); it keeps its own
background there.
- Color schemes are interpolated piecewise in sRGB, not taken from the
d3-scale-chromatic tables.
- labelExpr and the other expressions have format(value, specifier)
(d3-format), timeFormat() and utcFormat() (d3-time-format); an invalid
specifier is a render error. config.legend.labelExpr is not read, as in
Vega-Lite 6.
- Composite marks (boxplot, errorbar, errorband) report binned, aggregated,
or time-unit grouping channels and do not apply them.
- A shared legend shows the symbols of the first layer.
- Compositions drop more properties than Vega-Lite does; each is reported as
a warning.
- Delimited text is not type-inferred (as in Vega): cells stay strings
unless format.parse says otherwise.
- A line feed inside title text splits the title into lines, which Vega
itself does not do.
- Compared with vega-embed: no actions menu, no signals, no renderer choice,
and no config or datasets injection from the command line.

commands.name: vsdx
commands.description: Each drawing page is a page, drawn as an image.

options.name: --page
options.description: The page to draw, counted from 1 (default 1).

options.name: --all-pages
options.description:
Draw every page; for a drawing of more than one page the output must
contain {page} or be a directory.

options.name: --dpi
options.description:
Resolution in dots per inch (default 96, a whole number above 0 and at
most 2400).

options.name: --background
options.description: The color transparency is flattened over (white by default).

options.name: --strict
options.description:
Fail with unsupported-feature instead of drawing with an approximation.
Diagnostics and --strict:
- Each report is listed in diagnostics[] as {source: vsdx, severity:
unsupported, code: <token>} (without --json, also as an 'Unsupported:
<token>: <message>' line on standard error), once per distinct feature per
page. With --strict the first report fails with unsupported-feature.
vsdx-themed-color
A themed color was drawn neutral gray.
vsdx-geometry-spline-approximated
A curve was approximated by a polyline.
vsdx-geometry-row-<Type>
A geometry row was skipped.
Known differences from Visio:
- The approximations listed above, in particular neutral gray for themed
colors that cannot be resolved.
- Fonts that are not embedded come from the machine, so text can differ
between machines.
